title: DisplayServer functions return wrong values on macOS Tahoe with multiple monitors
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1] ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - macOS Tahoe (26.2.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M3 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M3 Pro (12 threads) - 18.00 GiB memory ### Issue description I'm using Godot on my Macbook Pro with external monitor (1440p). I have the Godot editor and Jetbrains Rider running on the external monitor. I'm using the external monitor as my primary display and my laptop's monitor is the extended display. In my project settings, Viewport Width is 1280 and Viewport Height is 720. All other Display > Window settings are the defaults. When I run my game from the editor _or_ from Rider, the window appears at half size. This is the core issue I'm trying to resolve. I've written a test script to debug why the window is appearing half size (see below). The output of various `DisplayServer` functions is different based on launch mode, however. It is also wrong in both cases. When I run with my test script from Rider, my extended monitor is correctly detected as the current screen, with screen id 0. But the resolution is reported as 2x what it should be. DPI looks reasonable though (the monitor is 27" diagonal, and 13.2" tall). It correctly reports screen scale (1, i.e., not HiDPI). Here's the output of the test script when running from Rider: ``` Screen count: 2 Window screen: 0 Window.Size (logical): (1280, 720) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(): (5120, 2880) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(currentScreen): (5120, 2880) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(0): (5120, 2880) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(1): (3024, 1964) DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(): 109 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(currentScreen): 109 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(0): 109 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(1): 256 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(): 1 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0): 1 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0): 1 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(1): 2 Viewport visible rect: (1280, 720) Viewport texture size: (1280, 720) ``` When I run it from the editor, almost all the values are wrong. `DisplayServer.GetScreenCount()` only reports one screen, although calling functions like `DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize()` with screenId 1 doesn't fail, it just returns (0,0). It seems to be treating my laptop monitor as the primary, based on the output of `DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale()`. Here's the output when running from the editor: ``` Screen count: 1 Window screen: 0 Window.Size (logical): (1280, 720) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(): (1280, 720) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(currentScreen): (1280, 720) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(0): (1280, 720) DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(1): (0, 0) DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(): 96 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(currentScreen): 96 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(0): 96 DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(1): 72 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(): 2 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0): 2 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0): 2 DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(1): 1 Viewport visible rect: (1280, 720) Viewport texture size: (1280, 720) ``` Here's the test script, which I've attached to the root node of my scene: ```c# public partial class Root : Node { public override void _Ready() { var w = GetWindow(); var vp = GetViewport(); var currentScreen = GetWindow().CurrentScreen; var currentScreenScale = DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(currentScreen); GD.Print($"Screen count: {DisplayServer.GetScreenCount()}"); GD.Print($"Window screen: {currentScreen}"); GD.Print($"Window.Size (logical): {w.Size}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize()}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(currentScreen): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(currentScreen)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(0): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(0)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(1): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetSize(1)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi()}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(currentScreen): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(currentScreen)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(0): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(0)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(1): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetDpi(1)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale()}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale({currentScreen}): {currentScreenScale}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(0)}"); GD.Print($"DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(1): {DisplayServer.ScreenGetScale(1)}"); GD.Print($"Viewport visible rect: {vp.GetVisibleRect().Size}"); GD.Print($"Viewport texture size: {vp.GetTexture().GetSize()}"); } } ``` Here's the output of `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType`: ```bash mike@Mac Development % system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType Graphics/Displays: Apple M3 Pro: Chipset Model: Apple M3 Pro Type: GPU Bus: Built-In Total Number of Cores: 18 Vendor: Apple (0x106b) Metal Support: Metal 4 Displays: DELL U2717D: Resolution: 2560 x 1440 (QHD/WQHD - Wide Quad High Definition) UI Looks like: 2560 x 1440 @ 60.00Hz Main Display: Yes Mirror: Off Online: Yes Rotation: Supported Color LCD: Display Type: Built-in Liquid Retina XDR Display Resolution: 3024 x 1964 Retina Mirror: Off Online: Yes Automatically Adjust Brightness: Yes Connection Type: Internal ``` This may be related to the same root cause as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/110106, although on a different OS. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create new project with Forward+ pipeline. 2. Set window size in project settings (optional). 3. Add Root script as attached above (optional; to reproduce debug output). 4. Launch game from editor or IDE. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [window-size-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25170390/window-size-issue.zip)
